title: EWCR v2 — Refusal record
description: Freezes architecture-c9070637.md §2.5 (evidence of correct refusal: no side effect, durable record), §7.4 (refusal leaves the instance at its node with a recovery requirement; stale-position / conflict refusals for racing proposals), and the refusal routes of §13 scenarios 1–8, 11–13, 15–16, 18–20. reason_code values map one-to-one onto those scenarios. v2 (T-5179, operator decision 2026-11-16) adds the refusal routes of the accepted scenarios N-1 and N-2 (accepted-scenarios.md): reason_code privilege_exceeds_profile with its privilege_excess record, and N-1 / N-2 as scenario_refs values. Everything else is as in v1.

instance_id.description: null only when refusing instance creation itself (§13 #1).

identity.description: Per-agent authenticated identity. Host identity alone is refused as ambiguous (arch §7.3, §13 #12).

auth_ref.description: Opaque, versioned reference into a registered catalogue. Never a path, shell string, or secret value (arch §6.2.1, §6.5).

refused_by.description: Runner identity. Exactly one privileged runner admits or refuses (§7.3).

reason_code.description: privilege_exceeds_profile is new in v2 (N-2): the resolved binding can do more than the node's declared capability profile allows. scope_mismatch (repository/worktree scope) and capability_unsupported (the provider cannot do the thing) name different axes.

scenario_refs.description: Acceptance scenarios this refusal is evidence for: architecture-c9070637.md §13 numbers (1–20), or, new in v2, the ids of scenarios accepted after §13 was frozen (accepted-scenarios.md). N-1 and N-2 are ids, not §13 numbers: §13 is not renumbered.

capability_profile_ref.description: The capability profile the node declares. Opaque catalogue reference (arch §6.2.1).

binding_ref.description: The secret binding that was resolved. Opaque reference, never the secret value (arch §6.5).

excess.description: Each privilege the resolved binding carries that the profile does not allow, by name. Never a secret value.

privilege_excess.description: privilege_exceeds_profile only (N-2): names the excess, so the record says what was refused and not only that something was.

side_effect.description: A refusal is by definition before side effect (§7.4). A record claiming otherwise is invalid.

ledger_position.description: Position at which the refusal itself was appended — refusals are ledger entries, not log lines.

expected_position.description: stale_position only: the position the loser proposed against.
